purpose: Compare analysis with and without checked-code retention and validate every public arena and graph edge.
properties: Identical accepted declaration IR, compared by its complete Debug representation.
Identical error offset and message for rejected inputs, except explicit checked-code resource limits.
Every typed ID resolves in the owning immutable graph; stored source spans and fragments are UTF-8 boundaries within the input.
Arena-once validation covers scopes, declarations, references, expressions and conversions, statements, initializers, runtime bounds, prototype ownership, and typeof operands.

input_policy.invalid_utf8: Rejected before analysis; no valid-prefix truncation.

origins: Checked-in checked and semantic seeds, with valid trailing comments selecting every target profile.
Previously compiler-preprocessed c-testsuite cases; the pinned origin and license metadata are recorded in corpus/conformance/c-testsuite.json.
The first run saved corpus and original failure artifact.

finding.kind: Diagnostic parity assertion; not an AddressSanitizer memory violation.
finding.fix: Report the ordinary constant-evaluation error before recording successful expressions. Preserve bounds and typeof operand evaluation contexts created while evaluating; reuse cached types and scopes.
regressions: Enum, array-bound, static-assert and bitfield diagnostics on all five target profiles.
Optional and unevaluated runtime bounds inside constant type queries.
No duplicate type definitions or statement-expression scopes while recording successful constant queries.

limits: The run counts fuzzer inputs, including invalid bytes and rejected C; it does not count accepted programs or independently verified compiler outputs.
The target selector distributes mutations across five target profiles; this is one native Linux ASan process, not execution on five operating systems or architectures.

The 224-input supplementary scan checks retention parity on already preprocessed text. Native preprocessor typedefs can be unsuitable for another profile, so matching rejections are retained in its report.
A clean bounded mutation run does not establish complete memory safety, C conformance, runtime semantics, or leak freedom.
